questions.q: What two fields make up a route in a route table?
options: A destination CIDR block and a target
A source IP and a port range
A priority number and a protocol
A subnet ID and an Availability Zone
questions.explain: A route is simply a destination CIDR (what traffic it matches) and a target (where that traffic is sent).

questions.q: What is the local route that appears in every route table?
options: A route to the internet that you can remove if unneeded
A route only present in the default VPC
An automatic, undeletable route for the VPC's own CIDR block, enabling all subnets to reach each other
A placeholder route that does nothing until configured
questions.explain: Every route table is created with a local route for the VPC's CIDR, and it can't be edited or deleted.

questions.q: Where does a NAT Gateway have to be placed?
options: Directly attached to the VPC with no subnet
In the same private subnet it provides outbound access for
In a public subnet, not the private subnet it serves
In any subnet, public or private, with no restriction
questions.explain: A NAT Gateway needs its own Elastic IP and lives in a public subnet, separate from the private subnet whose traffic it forwards.

questions.q: Why can a private-subnet instance behind a NAT Gateway download a software update, but a server on the internet can't open a new connection into that instance?
options: A NAT Gateway only forwards traffic that is a response to a connection the private instance initiated, never unsolicited inbound traffic
There's no real difference — both directions are equally open
NAT Gateways only work with HTTPS traffic, not package downloads
The NAT Gateway blocks all outbound traffic too, so neither direction actually works
questions.explain: A NAT Gateway enables outbound-initiated connections and their return traffic, but it never accepts a new inbound connection from the internet.

questions.q: In a private subnet's route table, what typically changes compared to a public subnet's table?
options: The 0.0.0.0/0 route's target is a NAT Gateway ID instead of an Internet Gateway ID
The destination CIDR for internet traffic changes to 10.0.0.0/16
There is no 0.0.0.0/0 route at all in either table
The local route for the VPC's CIDR is removed
questions.explain: Both tables can have a 0.0.0.0/0 route; what differs is the target — nat- for outbound-only, igw- for full internet reachability.
